speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Law (a) whether the Ministry can provide assistance to claimants to seek recourse from retailers who ignore and refuse to comply with the enforcement order of the Small Claims Tribunal (SCT); and (b) whether the SCT has the means to carry out enforcement actions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Claimants who wish to enforce an order of the SCT also have the following means of assistance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: More information on the eligibility criteria can be found at the LAB E-Services Portal on the Ministry of Law’s (MinLaw's) website.

speaker: The Minister of State for Law (Mr Murali Pillai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: More information on legal assistance can be found on MinLaw’s website link to “Legal Support Resources Available to Members of the Public”.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: She felt helpless and was told that she had to go and seek legal advice, which defeats the purpose of why we have the SCT for small claims.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, whether can there be more of this hand-holding, especially for the seniors, to be able to ultimately get their claims back, which is what the whole effort is all about.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: We seek his cooperation to bring to the attention of the resident these avenues and hopefully, through this, she will get the assistance that she needs.
